subject: general
question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹5,290 in 2 years and to ₹6,083.50 in 3 years. If interest is compounded annually, then the rate of interest per annum is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When interest is **compounded annually**, the interest earned in the 3rd year is simply the interest on the **amount** at the end of the 2ⁿd year.

Rate % = [(Difference between successive amounts) ÷ (Preceding amount)] × 100

Rate % = [(6083.50 − 5290) ÷ 5290] × 100

Rate % = (793.50 ÷ 5290) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹5,290

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹6,083.50

**Formula Used:**

Aₙ = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ce85c1fa50a1c3e7a8594427e675fced8b3dbf8140c89738eca2238bffda747.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₃ / A₂ = [P(1 + R/100)³] / [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 6083.50 / 5290 = (1 + R/100)

⇒ 1.15 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1.15 − 1 = 0.15

⇒ R = 0.15 × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest for Successive Years

If amounts for two consecutive years (n and n+1) are given, the rate R = [(Aₙ₊₁ − Aₙ) ÷ Aₙ] × 100.

Difference between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by D = P × (R/100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n.
